description.narrative:
The overall goal of the SCII project is: The resilience of communities, institutions and ecosystems in the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) region enhanced. Phase 2 of the SCII project will address the following outcome areas:
Outcome 1: Optimized Implementation of IDDRSI Consolidated.
Outcome 2. Analytical Capacities and Institutional Mechanisms for Food Security, Nutrition Information and Resilience Building in the IGAD Region Strengthened.

Syftet med detta bidrag är att konsolidera genomförandet av IGAD´s Initiativ för motståndskraft mot torkkatastrofer och hållbarhets genom att fortsatt stärka den kapaciteten i medlemsstaternas institutioner i deras utveckling av resultatbaserade system och i dess genomförande där planering, övervakning, utvärdering, finansiering och rapportering är överensstämmer och är resultatorienterad. I användandet av resultaten av denna insats så ska IGAD stärka sin analytiska kapacitet och institutionella mekanism för livsmedelssäkerhet, näringsupplysning och byggande av motståndskraft i regionen.

The purpose of this contribution is to consolidate implementation of IGAD Drought Disaster Resilience & Sustainability Initiative through further strengthening the institutional capacity of IGAD Member State institutions to develop a result-based management system where planning, monitoring, evaluation, budgeting and reporting are coherent and result oriented. In addition, IGAD will also strengthen analytical capacities and institutional mechanisms for Food Security, Nutrition Information and Resilience Building in the IGAD Region.

sector.narrative: Food security policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The Support to the Coordination and Implementation of IDDRSI (SCII) Project Phase 2 represents a critical initiative aimed at enhancing the resilience of communities, institutions, and ecosystems across the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) region. Building on the successes of its first phase (20192023), this phase, continues to address the multifaceted challenges posed by climate variability, food insecurity, and socio-economic vulnerabilities. The contribution aligns with the broader objectives of the IGAD Drought Disaster Resilience and Sustainability Initiative (IDDRSI), which seeks to foster sustainable development and disaster preparedness. The IGAD region, comprising eight member states, faces recurrent droughts, floods, and conflicts that exacerbate food insecurity, displacement, and poverty. These challenges are further compounded by weak institutional capacities, fragmented coordination mechanisms, and limited access to timely and actionable data. In response, the contribution focuses on two primary objectives: strengthening Results-Based Management (RBM) systems for IDDRSI implementation and enhancing analytical capacities for food security, nutrition, and climate resilience. In this regard the contribution aims to institutionalize adaptive governance, improve data-driven decision-making, and promote cross-border collaboration to address systemic vulnerabilities.
Significant progress was made toward the optimized implementation of IDDRSI. A pivotal highlight was the tailored training coupled with a field visit on survey methodology, which equipped monitoring and evaluation experts with crucial skills for enhancing the result-based management systems of Country Programming Papers (CPPs) that enables member states t conduct assessments to evaluate ongoing resilience projects, generating vital recommendations for further development and infrastructural improvements.
The technical assistance provided through the National Expert Panels (NEPs), which enables member states to effectively validate CPPs and harmonize resilience indicators focusing on gender inclusivity, improving data-sharing and resource mobilization for conflict-sensitive programming. Timely and critical updates on food security were disseminated through monthly FSNWG reports, which facilitated early warning alerts in response to the anticipated El Niño phenomenon. The Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum (GHACOF) further acted as a major platform enabling climate information dissemination and stakeholder engagement. In general institutional governance has been strengthened, with steering committees ensuring that CPPs aligned with regional priorities in addressing drought risk management and multi-sectoral coordination.
Despite notable successes, the project faced challenges related to political instability, funding gaps, and staffing transitions. The retirement of several National IDDRSI Coordinators necessitated prompt recruitment and induction to preserve project momentum. Furthermore, discussions with stakeholders underscored the need for diversified funding strategies and enhanced data-driven decision-making frameworks.
In conclusion, the project has made significant strides in enhancing resilience in the IGAD region, notably by improving institutional capacity and optimizing implementation frameworks.
